# backup_tool

[← Command index](README.md)

Copy, encrypt, decrypt or archive a directory tree into another directory.

## Synopsis

```
backup_tool [options]
```

## Description

Copies every file under the source directory to the same relative path under the
destination. With `-r Encrypt` each file is encrypted with GPG (AES-256) and stored as
the MD5 of its filename plus `.enc`, with the real filename kept inside the encrypted
file; `-r Decrypt` reverses this and restores the real filename. Files that are already
in the target form (already encrypted, or not encrypted) are copied as they are.

With `-b Archive` the tool instead looks two levels down: each directory at
`<source>/<A>/<B>` becomes a 7z archive at `<destination>/<A>/<B>.7z`, split into
4092 MB volumes. Files not inside such a directory are not archived, and `-r` is ignored.

Source and destination are each resolved the same way. A path given with `-i`/`-o`
that exists is used as is. Otherwise the path is built from a root and the game
options: `<root>/Gaming/<supercategory>/<category>/<subcategory>/<offset>`, stopping
at the first one not given. The root is `--input_locker_base`/`--output_locker_base`
if given and it exists, otherwise the mount path of the `-l`/`-d` locker. When a
locker base is given, `-i`/`-o` is ignored for that side.

The encryption passphrase comes from configuration, not the command line: the
destination locker's passphrase when encrypting, the source locker's when decrypting,
falling back to the general locker passphrase.

## Options

### Paths

| Option | Description |
|--------|-------------|
| `-i, --input_path <input_path>` | Source directory, used as is when it exists. |
| `-o, --output_path <output_path>` | Destination directory, used as is when it exists. |
| `--input_locker_base <input_locker_base>` | Directory to use as the source locker root instead of the `-l` locker's mount path; the game options are resolved under it and `-i` is ignored. |
| `--output_locker_base <output_locker_base>` | Directory to use as the destination locker root instead of the `-d` locker's mount path; the game options are mirrored under it, the destination is created if missing, and `-o` is ignored. |

### Game path

| Option | Description |
|--------|-------------|
| `-u, --game_supercategory <game_supercategory>` | Game supercategory folder under `Gaming` used to build a locker path. Default: `Roms`. Allowed: `Assets`, `Emulators`, `Roms`, `DLC`, `Updates`, `Tags`, `Saves`, `Setup`, `Installs`. |
| `-c, --game_category <game_category>` | Game category folder under the supercategory. Allowed: `Computer`, `Microsoft`, `Nintendo`, `Other`, `Sony`. |
| `-s, --game_subcategory <game_subcategory>` | Game subcategory (platform) folder under the category; used only with `-c`. Allowed: `Amazon Games`, `Disc`, `Epic Games`, `GOG`, `Humble Bundle`, `Itchio`, `Legacy Games`, `Puppet Combo`, `Red Candle`, `Square Enix`, `Steam`, `Zoom`, `Microsoft MSX`, `Microsoft Xbox`, `Microsoft Xbox 360`, `Microsoft Xbox 360 GOD`, `Microsoft Xbox 360 XBLA`, `Microsoft Xbox 360 XIG`, `Microsoft Xbox One`, `Microsoft Xbox One GOD`, `Nintendo 3DS`, `Nintendo 3DS Apps`, `Nintendo 3DS eShop`, `Nintendo 64`, `Nintendo Amiibo`, `Nintendo DS`, `Nintendo DSi`, `Nintendo Famicom`, `Nintendo Game Boy`, `Nintendo Game Boy Advance`, `Nintendo Game Boy Advance e-Reader`, `Nintendo Game Boy Color`, `Nintendo Gamecube`, `Nintendo NES`, `Nintendo SNES`, `Nintendo SNES MSU-1`, `Nintendo Super Famicom`, `Nintendo Super Game Boy`, `Nintendo Super Game Boy Color`, `Nintendo Switch`, `Nintendo Switch eShop`, `Nintendo Virtual Boy`, `Nintendo Wii`, `Nintendo Wii U`, `Nintendo Wii U eShop`, `Nintendo WiiWare`, `Apple iOS`, `Apple MacOS 8`, `Arcade`, `Atari 800`, `Atari 2600`, `Atari 5200`, `Atari 7800`, `Atari Jaguar`, `Atari Jaguar CD`, `Atari Lynx`, `Bandai WonderSwan`, `Bandai WonderSwan Color`, `Coleco ColecoVision`, `Commodore 64`, `Commodore Amiga`, `Google Android`, `Magnavox Odyssey 2`, `Mattel Intellivision`, `NEC PC-Engine`, `NEC PC-Engine CD`, `NEC SuperGrafx`, `NEC TurboGrafx-16`, `NEC TurboGrafx CD`, `Nokia N-Gage`, `Panasonic 3DO`, `Philips CDi`, `SNK Neo Geo Pocket Color`, `Sega 32X`, `Sega CD`, `Sega CD 32X`, `Sega Dreamcast`, `Sega Game Gear`, `Sega Genesis`, `Sega Master System`, `Sega Saturn`, `Sinclair ZX Spectrum`, `Texas Instruments TI-99-4A`, `Tiger Game.com`, `Sony PlayStation`, `Sony PlayStation 2`, `Sony PlayStation 3`, `Sony PlayStation 4`, `Sony PlayStation Network - PlayStation 3`, `Sony PlayStation Network - PlayStation 4`, `Sony PlayStation Network - PlayStation Portable`, `Sony PlayStation Network - PlayStation Portable Minis`, `Sony PlayStation Network - PlayStation Vita`, `Sony PlayStation Portable`, `Sony PlayStation Portable Video`, `Sony PlayStation Vita`. |
| `-g, --game_offset <game_offset>` | Further relative path under the subcategory, such as one game's folder; used only with `-s`. |

### Behavior

| Option | Description |
|--------|-------------|
| `-b, --backup_type <Copy\|Archive>` | `Copy` copies files one by one; `Archive` packs each second-level directory into a split 7z archive. Default: `Copy`. Allowed: `Copy`, `Archive`. |
| `-l, --source_locker <source_locker>` | Locker whose mount path is the source root, and whose passphrase is used when decrypting. Default: `Local`. Allowed: `All`, `Local`, `Hetzner`, `Gdrive`, `External`. |
| `-d, --dest_locker <dest_locker>` | Locker whose mount path is the destination root, and whose passphrase is used when encrypting. Default: `Local`. Allowed: `All`, `Local`, `Hetzner`, `Gdrive`, `External`. |
| `-w, --exclude_paths <exclude_paths>` | Comma-separated path prefixes, relative to the source; files whose relative path starts with one are left out. |
| `-e, --skip_existing` | Skip a file when its destination already exists. |
| `-a, --skip_identical` | Skip a file when its destination already exists with the same content. |
| `-r, --cryption_type <None\|Encrypt\|Decrypt>` | Encrypt or decrypt each file while copying; `None` copies files unchanged. Applies to `Copy` only. Default: `None`. Allowed: `None`, `Encrypt`, `Decrypt`. |
| `--delete_original` | Delete each source file after it has been encrypted or decrypted; has no effect on a plain copy. |

### Common options

| Option | Description |
|--------|-------------|
| `-v, --verbose` | Enable verbose mode. |
| `-p, --pretend_run` | Do a pretend run with no permanent changes. |
| `-x, --exit_on_failure` | Enable exit on failure mode. |
| `--no-preview` | Skip the preview confirmation prompt. |

## Examples

### Copy one directory into another

```bash
backup_tool -i /path/to/source -o /path/to/destination
```

### Preview a copy without changing anything

```bash
backup_tool -i /path/to/source -o /path/to/destination -p -v
```

### Encrypt files while copying them to a backup directory

```bash
backup_tool -i /path/to/local/files -o /path/to/backup -r Encrypt
```

### Decrypt files and remove the encrypted originals

```bash
backup_tool -i /path/to/encrypted -o /path/to/decrypted -r Decrypt --delete_original
```

### Resume an interrupted copy, skipping files already at the destination

```bash
backup_tool -i /path/to/source -o /path/to/destination -e
```

### Copy the local locker's Nintendo Switch ROMs to an existing directory

```bash
backup_tool -o /mnt/external/backup -u Roms -c Nintendo -s "Nintendo Switch"
```

### Decrypt Nintendo Switch ROMs from the mounted Hetzner locker into the local locker

```bash
backup_tool -l Hetzner -d Local -u Roms -c Nintendo -s "Nintendo Switch" -r Decrypt
```

### Encrypt local Nintendo Switch ROMs into the mounted Hetzner locker

```bash
backup_tool -l Local -d Hetzner -u Roms -c Nintendo -s "Nintendo Switch" -r Encrypt
```

### Decrypt one game's updates onto an external drive, mirroring the locker layout

```bash
backup_tool -l Hetzner --output_locker_base /media/user/External -u Updates -c Microsoft -s "Microsoft Xbox" -g "Halo 2 (USA)" -r Decrypt
```

### Mirror between two external drives, skipping unchanged files

```bash
backup_tool --input_locker_base /media/user/Drive1 --output_locker_base /media/user/Drive2 -u Roms -c Nintendo -s "Nintendo Switch" -a
```

### Archive each game directory into split 7z files

```bash
backup_tool -i /path/to/source -o /path/to/archives -b Archive
```

## Notes

- A remote locker (`Hetzner`, `Gdrive`) must be mounted first with `sync_tool -a Mount -l <locker>`; the tool only reads and writes its mount path.
- `-u` defaults to `Roms`, so a source or destination that is not an existing `-i`/`-o` path always resolves under `Gaming/Roms` unless `-u` says otherwise.
- The source and destination must differ. A missing destination is created only when `--output_locker_base` is given and exists.
- Without `-x`, a plain copy that hits an I/O error on a file removes the partial copy, appends the source path to `copy_errors.txt` in the destination, and carries on. With `-x` the run stops instead.
- `-a` with `-r` decrypts the existing destination file to a temporary directory and compares contents, so unchanged files are not encrypted or decrypted again.
